paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God wants His people to come to Him the way HE says, not the way that feels handy. Instead of slaughtering animals out in the open fields, the Israelites were to bring their sacrifices to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting (Leviticus 17:4-5). God wasn't being picky about a parking spot. He was keeping His people close to Him and away from the goat demons they had been offering to (Leviticus 17:7).

Then comes the heart of it: "For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you to make atonement for your souls upon the altar; for it is the blood that makes atonement for the soul" (Leviticus 17:11). Read that slowly. Atonement is GOD's gift, not something we earn or invent. The blood was precious because life is precious, and He said so again and again, because when somebody repeats themselves that much, friend, you write it on your hand (Leviticus 17:12, 14).

So what does this mean for you today? Sin costs a life, and God Himself provided the way to cover it. That's why I thank Jesus every day for reaching into a dark drawer and finding me, because the Lamb gave His life to rescue people (Mark 10:45). And the same God who said "the life of all flesh is its blood" is the One who welcomes you in. Come to Him His way, friend, and you'll never be cut off.
